title: smallRNA_analysis
text:
Processing
Before the analysis, we did a few processing and filtering steps to remove non-relevant components such as adaptors, rRNA, tRNA, reads in low complexity regions,etc.

title: smallRNA_analysis
text:
Analysis
There are two main analysis I did:

Identify the mobile sRNA, i.e. smallRNA present in scion tissue (Sauvignon Blanc leaf) that presumed to be originated from the rootstock. To do this, we first align the reads to the scion genome (both haplotypes), take the unmapped reads and align to the respective rootstock genome (one haplotype).
Analyse the association of smallRNA reads with drought stress. For this, we map the reads to a concatenated reference genome of the scion and rootstock, perform clustering (both done within ShortStack) and run differential analysis on the result to identify clusters that are significantly associated with drought stress.


Identify mobile sRNA
First, filtered small RNA reads were mapped to the scion genome using bowtie. the unmapped reads were used to map to the rootstock genome
#Create bowtie-index
bowtie-build SB2.1_diploid_plusorg.fasta SB2.1_bowtie_build/SB2.1_diploid


#Map to scion genome
cd $DIR/
for i in *_nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz
do
base=$(basename "$i" _nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz)
bowtie --threads 8 -v 0 -a -m 50 --best --strata \
       --un $DIR/${base}.unaligned.SB.fq \
       --max $DIR/${base}.too_many.SB.fq \
       -S -x $ref_SB_hap1 \
       $DIR/${base}_nonchloro_SB.fastq.gz \
       | samtools sort -@8 | samtools view -b -@8 -o $DIR/${base}_SB_dip.sorted.aligned.bam
samtools index -@16 $DIR/${base}_SB_dip.sorted.aligned.bam
done

#Map unmapped reads to rootstock genome (e.g. 3309)
cd $DIR/
for i in *.unaligned.SB.fq
do
base=$(basename "$i" .unaligned.SB.fq)
bowtie --threads 8 -v 0 -a -m 50 --best --strata \
       --un $DIR2/3309/${base}.unaligned.SBdip_align.3309.fq \
       --max $DIR2/3309/${base}.too_many.SBdip_3309.fq \
       -S -x $ref_3309 \
       $DIR/${base}.unaligned.SB.fq \
       | samtools sort -@8 | samtools view -b -@8 -o $DIR2/3309/${base}_unmappedSBdip_map3309.sorted.aligned.bam
samtools index -@16 $DIR2/3309/${base}_unmappedSBdip_map3309.sorted.aligned.bam
done
Clustering was done using ShortStack

#clustering
ShortStack --bamfile file1.bam file2.bam ...filexx.bam \
--dicermin 20 --dicermax 24 --mincov 5 \
--genomefile ref.fa \
--known_miRNAs mirbase_vitis.fasta \
--outdir Result_DIR/


Association of small RNA with drought stress
For this, we use small RNA mapped to both scion and rootstock. Mapping and clustering was done using ShortStack. Shortstack also use bowtie for mapping, but has default setting that allows 1 mismatch. We modify the script manually to change the mismatch allowed to 0, according to this thread: https://github.com/MikeAxtell/ShortStack/issues/177

#Mapping and clustering
ShortStack --bamfile file1.bam file2.bam ...filexx.bam \
--dicermin 20 --dicermax 24 --mincov 5 \
--genomefile ref_SB_3309.fa \
--known_miRNAs mirbase_vitis.fasta \
--outdir Result_DIR/
Differential analysis was done using Deseq2, using the count.txt table output of shorstack

#Deseq2 library(DESeq2)
#| eval: false
counts <- read.table("count.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) 
rownames(counts) <- counts$Name 
locus_info <- counts[, c("Name", "Coords", "MIRNA")]

#Define samples 
sample_map <- list(control_baseline = c("control1_B", "control2_B", "control3_B"), 
                   treatment_baseline = c("treatment1_B","treatment2_B","treatment3_B"), 
                   control_stress = c("control1_S", "control2_S", "control3_S"), 
                   treatment_stress = c("treatment1_S","treatment2_S","treatment3_S"))

#Biological pairing 
pair_map <- c(control1_B = "C1", control1_S = "C1", 
              control1_B = "C2", control1_S = "C2", 
              control3_B = "C3", control3_S = "C3", 
              treatment1_B = "T1", treatment1_S = "T1", 
              treatment1_B = "T2", treatment1_S = "T2", 
              treatment3_B = "T3", treatment3_S = "T3",)

#Build sample metadata 
lookup <- do.call( rbind, 
                   lapply(names(sample_map), function(grp) { 
  parts <- strsplit(grp, "_")[[1]] 
  data.frame(
    id = sample_map[[grp]], 
    drought = parts[1], 
    timepoint = parts[2], 
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) }))

## Add biological pair ID

lookup$pair_id <- unname(pair_map[lookup$id])

#Identify columns in count matrix 
sample_ids <- sub("_.*", "", colnames(counts_mat_all)) 
keep_cols <- sample_ids %in% lookup$id 
counts_mat <- counts_mat_all[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE] 
sample_ids <- sample_ids[keep_cols] 
dim(counts_mat) 
colnames(counts_mat)

#Contruct coldata to be exactly same orders as counts 
coldata <- lookup[ match(sample_ids, lookup$id), c("drought", "timepoint", "pair_id")]

rownames(coldata) <- colnames(counts_mat)

#Confirm pairing 
cat("nPairing table:n") 
print(table(coldata$pair_id,coldata$timepoint)) 
pair_table <- table( coldata$pair_id,coldata$timepoint) 

stopifnot(all(pair_table[, "baseline"] == 1), all(pair_table[, "stress"] == 1))

## Each pair must belong to only one drought treatment

drought_check <- tapply(
  as.character(coldata$drought),
  coldata$pair_id,
  function(x) length(unique(x))
) 

stopifnot(all(drought_check == 1))

#Split miRNA vs siRNA 
mirna_ids <- locus_info$Name[locus_info$MIRNA == "Y"] 
sirna_ids <- locus_info$Name[locus_info$MIRNA == "N"]

counts_mirna <- counts_mat[
  rownames(counts_mat) %in% mirna_ids, 
  ,
  drop = FALSE]

counts_sirna <- counts_mat[
  rownames(counts_mat) %in% sirna_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE]

#Diff analysis, example for siRNA 
count_mat <- round(as.matrix(counts_sirna)) 
coldata <- as.data.frame(coldata)

coldata$ctrl_stress <- as.integer(coldata$drought == "control" & coldata$timepoint == "stress")
coldata$trt_stress <- as.integer(coldata$drought == "treatment" & coldata$timepoint == "stress")

#paired Wald model 
#(trt stress - trt baseline) - (ctrl stress - ctrl baseline)
#Positive LFC = treatment has a more positive stress response

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix( 
  countData = count_mat, 
  colData = coldata, 
  design = ~ pair_id + ctrl_stress + trt_stress)

dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts") 
sizeFactors(dds)
dds <- DESeq(dds) 
rn <- resultsNames(dds)

int_contrast <- setNames(rep(0, length(rn)), rn) 
int_contrast["trt_stress"] <- 1 
int_contrast["ctrl_stress"] <- -1

int_contrast

res_interaction <- results(dds, contrast = int_contrast) 
summary(res_interaction)

interaction_res <- as.data.frame(res_interaction) 
interaction_res$Name <- rownames(interaction_res)
interaction_res <- merge(interaction_res, locus_info, by = "Name", all.x = TRUE)
interaction_res <- interaction_res[order(interaction_res$padj, na.last = TRUE),]

write.csv(interaction_res,"res_interaction_wald_siRNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#Interaction DROUGHT x TIMEPOINT (LRT method) 
#Fit the design for DROUGHT x TIMEPOINT INTERACTION 
## Full : ~ pair_id + timepoint + trt_stress

dds_int_lrt <- DESeq(dd, test = "LRT", reduced = ~ pair_id + timepoint)

res_lrt_int <- results(dds_int_lrt) 
summary(res_lrt_int)

lrt_int_res <- as.data.frame(res_lrt_int) 
lrt_int_res$Name <- rownames(lrt_int_res)
lrt_int_res <- merge(lrt_int_res, locus_info, by = "Name", all.x = TRUE)
lrt_int_res <- lrt_int_res[order(lrt_int_res$padj, na.last = TRUE),]

write.csv(lrt_int_res,"res_interaction_LRT_siRNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#Interaction DROUGHT x TIMEPOINT INTERACTION (LfcShrink method) 
## Full : ~ pair_id + timepoint + trt_stress

res_int_shrunk <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "trt_stress", type = "apeglm") 
summary(res_int_shrunk)

res_int_shrunk_df <- as.data.frame(res_int_shrunk) 
res_int_shrunk_df$Name <- rownames(res_int_shrunk_df)
res_int_shrunk_df <- merge(res_int_shrunk_df, locus_info, by = "Name", all.x = TRUE)
res_int_shrunk_df <- res_int_shrunk_df[order(res_int_shrunk_df$padj, na.last = TRUE),]

write.csv(res_int_shrunk_df,"res_interaction_shrunk_siRNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Processing

Short read data (MGI) filtering
ml fastp/0.23.4-GCC-11.3.0


for i in *_1.fq.gz    
do
fastp --trim_front1   4     --trim_front2 4   --cut_right  --cut_mean_quality 25  --average_qual 30 --length_required  50  --fix_mgi_id --disable_adapter_trimming --in1 $i --out1 ${i%_1.fq.gz}_1.filtered.fq.gz  --in2   ${i%_1.fq.gz}_2.fq.gz --out2  ${i%_1.fq.gz}_2.filtered.fq.gz --thread 8 
echo "done processing $i"
done

#disabled adaptor trimming since no over-represented sequences found and not clear what sequences to use. 


Long read data (ONT) basecalling
#Data were basecalled using the 5mC,5hmC and 6mA in all contexts in super-accurate mode

SAMPLES=sample_sheet.csv
POD5=/DIR_pod5/
OUTFILE=Sample_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.bam
DEMUX=Project_demux
dorado basecaller sup,5mC_5hmC,6mA --sample-sheet $SAMPLES --kit-name SQK-NBD114-96  --device 'cuda:all'  --recursive $POD5 --resume-from $OUTFILE > ${OUTFILE%.bam}.resumed.bam
dorado demux --sample-sheet $SAMPLES  --output-dir $DEMUX  --no-classify $OUTFILE

# Convert to fq and merge
module load pigz/2.7 SAMtools/1.19-GCC-12.3.0

bam=sample.bam
fq=sample.fastq.gz
samtools fastq -T "*" -@ 8 $bam | pigz -p 8  -9 >  $fq

cat sample1.fastq.gz sample2.fastq.gz .. > combined.fastq.gz

# RUn stats with seqkit stats or seqkit stats -a


Filtering
#Filter with chopper or seqtk
#We can apply different criteria of filtering, e.g. exclude reads with Q <10 and length < 1kb

gunzip -c sample.fastq.gz | chopper --minlength 8000 --threads 16 | gzip > sample.filtered.fastq.gz

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Dorado Correct
We ran dorado correct for read correction, but also run assembly with the simplex read directly, and will compare the result for both approach

module load Dorado/0.9.0

dorado correct sample.filtered.fastq.gz --to-paf -t 32 -x cpu > sample.paf
dorado correct sample.fastq.gz --from-paf sample.paf -x cuda:all -t 32 > sample_corrected.fasta

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Genome assembly
Assembly was done using hifiasm, and run with different options: 1. from dorado corrected reads (>8kb) 2. from simplex non-corrected reads (include all >1kb >Q10 reads) –> using –ont argument which is available in later version of hifiasm

# Install hifiasm

git clone https://github.com/chhylp123/hifiasm
cd hifiasm && make

export PATH=$PATH:/nesi/nobackup/brins03581/Cen/tools/hifiasm

# Run hifiasm 

hifiasm -t 32 --ont -o /sample_simplex_ONT --chem-c 2 sample.filtered.fastq

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
First QC check on assembly
Perform QC on each assembly separately:

simplex (3309 hap1 and hap2; 1103P hap1 and hap2)
corrected (3309 hap1 and hap2; 1103P hap1 and hap2)

QCs: Quast: for contiguity (no. of contigs, N50, total length among others) compleasm: for completeness (BUSCO genes, missing genes) Dgenies for comparison with other assemblies (e.g. PN40024 T2T) Mercury: for accuracy (QV, also completeness)

# Quast
ml QUAST/5.2.0-gimkl-2022a

DIR=rootstock_2025
quast.py assembly.fasta

# COmpleasm

module load compleasm/0.2.5-gimkl-2022a 

#Run on each hap1 and hap2 separately
compleasm.py run -a simplex.hap1.p_ctg.fa  -o simplex_hap1  -t 8 -l eudicots

compleasm.py run -a simplex.hap2.p_ctg.fa  -o simplex_hap2  -t 8 -l eudicots

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Purge duplication
Run for each haplotype separately, Use this: https://github.com/dfguan/purge_dups
module load minimap2/2.28-GCC-12.3.0

#1103P_correct_hap2
cd /1103P_corr_hap2/
minimap2 -x lr:hq -t 8 /1103P_corrected.bp.hap2.p_ctg.fa /1103P_combined_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.8kbplus.filtered.fastq |  gzip -c - > 1103P_corrected2.hap2.paf.gz

/tools/purge_dups/bin/pbcstat 1103P_corrected2.hap2.paf.gz

/tools/purge_dups/bin/calcuts PB.stat > cutoffs 2>calcults.log

/tools/purge_dups/bin/split_fa 1103P_corrected.bp.hap2.p_ctg.fa > 1103P_corrected_hap2.fa.split

minimap2 -xasm5 -DP  1103P_corrected_hap2.fa.split  1103P_corrected_hap2.fa.split | gzip -c - > 1103P_corrected_hap2.fa.split.self.paf.gz

/tools/purge_dups/bin/purge_dups -2 -T cutoffs -c PB.base.cov 1103P_corrected_hap2.fa.split.self.paf.gz > dups.bed 2> purge_dups.log

/tools/purge_dups/bin/get_seqs -e dups.bed /1103P_corrected.bp.hap2.p_ctg.fa

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Filter with dgenies
After purged dups, QC based on quast and compleasm still look good, but no. of contigs still quite high for some of the assemblies.
Next steps:

Map the assemblies to PN40024 T2T genome assembly on dgenies (https://dgenies.toulouse.inra.fr/run)
Download the paf files
Filter on excel, retain only contigs with residue matches > 50kb
save these (the contig names) on txt file, and use this to filter the genome assembly using seqkit
re-do QC on these filtered assemblies

# Filter assembly using seqkit

module load SeqKit/2.4.0

seqkit grep -f /1103P_corr_hap1_purged_dgenies.txt /1103P_corr_hap1_purged.fa -o /purged_dup_filtered_dgenies/1103P_corr_hap1_purged_dgenies.fa

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Polish with NextPolish2
To increased accuracy, next step is to polish the assembly.
We use NextPolish2 (https://github.com/Nextomics/NextPolish2)
Steps as follow, replace the HiFi with the filtered ONT reads (Q20), and use winnowmap.

# Prepare reads (Winnowmap)
use these ONT reads:
/3309_combined_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.Q20.filtered.fastq.gz
/1103P_combined_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.Q20.filtered.fastq.gz

seqkit stats -a /3309_combined_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.Q20.filtered.fastq.gz

#Meryl
meryl count k=15 output 3309_hap1_merylDB /3309_simplex_hap1_purged_dgenies.fa

meryl count k=15 output 3309_hap2_merylDB /3309_simplex_hap2_purged_dgenies.fa

meryl print greater-than distinct=0.9998 1103P_hap1_merylDB > 1103P_hap1_repetitive_k15.txt

meryl print greater-than distinct=0.9998 1103P_hap2_merylDB > 1103P_hap2_repetitive_k15.txt

# Winnowmap

module load Winnowmap/2.03-GCC-11.3.0
winnowmap -t 5 -W 3309_hap1_repetitive_k15.txt -ax map-ont /3309_simplex_hap1_purged_dgenies.fa /3309_combined_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.Q20.filtered.fastq.gz | samtools sort -o 3309_hap1_winnowmap.map.sort.bam -
samtools index 3309_hap1_winnowmap.map.sort.bam

winnowmap -t 5 -W 3309_hap2_repetitive_k15.txt -ax map-ont /3309_simplex_hap2_purged_dgenies.fa /3309_combined_sup_5mC_5hmC_6mA.0.9.0.Q20.filtered.fastq.gz | samtools sort -o 3309_hap2_winnowmap.map.sort.bam -
samtools index 3309_hap2_winnowmap.map.sort.bam

# Prepare k-mer profile (yak)
module load yak/0.1

#use kmer=19 as per Annabel's suggestion, as when run mercury
#https://github.com/Nextomics/NextPolish2

#Yak
cd /nextpolish2
yak count -o 3309_k31.yak -k 31 -b 37 <(zcat /MGI_data/IB008_sample1_1.filtered.fq.gz) <(zcat /IB008_sample1_2.filtered.fq.gz)

yak count -o 3309_k21.yak -k 21 -b 37 <(zcat /MGI_data/IB008_sample1_1.filtered.fq.gz) <(zcat /IB008_sample1_2.filtered.fq.gz)

##Nextpolish2

module load NextPolish2/0.2.1-foss-2023a

nextPolish2 -t 8 /3309_hap1_winnowmap.map.sort.bam /3309_simplex_hap1_purged_dgenies.fa /nextpolish2/yak_repeat/3309_k21.yak /nextpolish2/yak_repeat/3309_k21.yak > /nextpolish2/polished/3309_simplex_hap1_repeat_polished.fa

nextPolish2 -t 8 /3309_hap2_winnowmap.map.sort.bam /3309_simplex_hap2_purged_dgenies.fa /nextpolish2/yak_repeat/3309_k21.yak /nextpolish2/yak_repeat/3309_k21.yak > /nextpolish2/polished/3309_simplex_hap2_repeat_polished.fa

title: Genome assembly of Roostock - 3309 and 1103P
text:
Scaffold with Ragtag
ml Miniconda3
source activate /nesi/project/brins03581/env/ragtag
REF=PN40024.T21.fa 
cd /nextpolish2/polished/

for i in *.fa
do
ragtag.py scaffold -o /nextpolish2/ragtag${i}_ragtag_nostringency -t 8 $REF $i
done


This uses the default stringency setting (which is -1 0.2)
Also tried with different stringency (0.6; 0.8; 0.9)
